tasks.title: Widen PermissionMode to four modes across the contract, the runtime guard, the IPC validator, and the SQLite CHECK constraint
acceptance: `PermissionMode` in `src/shared/contracts/events.ts` is `'default' | 'acceptEdits' | 'plan' | 'bypassPermissions'`, and the block comment above it is rewritten to state the new four-value product surface â€” it must no longer read as a three-value restriction, because that comment is what a future reader treats as authoritative. This is the contract change the orchestrator escalated at Gate 2; if it was NOT approved, this task stops and reports rather than proceeding.

`ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES` in `src/main/pod/options.ts` contains exactly the four values, `isAllowedPermissionMode('acceptEdits')` returns true, and `createPodRunner` accepts a Pod constructed with `acceptEdits` without throwing.

The compile-time exhaustiveness guard in `src/main/store/schema.ts` still resolves to `never`: `type _UncoveredPermissionMode = Exclude<PermissionMode, (typeof PERMISSION_MODES)[number]>` compiles, proving `PERMISSION_MODES` and the union did not drift apart.

A NEW migration (version 2) widens the `pods.permission_mode` CHECK constraint. `MIGRATION_1` is NOT edited: its DDL is pinned to the literal three-mode list it shipped with, honouring the `MIGRATIONS` docblock's "append new entries; never edit a shipped one". A test asserts migration 1's SQL text is byte-identical to the version in `git show main:src/main/store/schema.ts`.

Migration 2 preserves data: a test opens a v1 database containing pods, lanes, and events, runs `migrate()`, and asserts every row survives with identical values, foreign keys intact, and `schema_version` = 2. If the table is rebuilt to change the constraint, `PRAGMA foreign_keys` handling is proven correct by that test rather than assumed.

`migrate()` remains idempotent at version 2 â€” calling it twice on the same file leaves schema and data unchanged â€” and still throws `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` when the on-disk version exceeds `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`.

Inserting `permission_mode = 'acceptEdits'` succeeds after migration and inserting an unlisted value (e.g. `'dontAsk'`, `'auto'`, `'manual'` â€” all accepted by the CLI but deliberately NOT exposed by Orcastrate) is still rejected by the CHECK constraint. `tests/unit/store/schema.test.ts`'s current assertion that `acceptEdits` is rejected is updated, not deleted, so the negative case still has a named mode behind it.

`requirePermissionMode` in `src/main/ipc/validate.ts` accepts `acceptEdits` and its `INVALID_ARGUMENT` message enumerates all four modes verbatim; the existing `tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts` cases that used `acceptEdits` as a known-invalid value are re-pointed at a value that is still invalid (`'dontAsk'`), so the malformed-input path keeps its coverage.

`tests/unit/pod/options.test.ts`'s 'does not accept acceptEdits' tests are inverted rather than removed: they now assert `acceptEdits` IS accepted at construction and through `setPermissionMode`, and a still-unexposed mode is rejected at both.
Nothing outside the permission-mode surface changes: the diff touches no lane routing, no PodManager wiring, no event shape, and no renderer file.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both pass.

tasks.title: Route system/task_progress to its own Calf lane, and document the canUseTool attribution race
acceptance: A `system` message with subtype `task_progress` produces a transcript event whose `laneId` is the lane registered for that message's `tool_use_id`, resolved through the router's existing `byToolUseId` index â€” not the Matriarch. Today `routeSystem` sends every `system` message to the Matriarch, which leaves a background Calf's lane empty while the Matriarch fills with progress lines about a lane the user is reading elsewhere.

Fallback is explicit and tested: a `task_progress` whose `tool_use_id` is absent, or names no registered lane, still lands on the Matriarch and is never dropped. Every event the router emits continues to carry a non-null `laneId`.

The ordering guarantee the existing suite asserts is preserved: routing a `task_progress` to a not-yet-materialized Calf materializes it first, so `lane_opened` still precedes every event carrying that lane's id. This is the hazard the two-phase lifecycle exists for, and the fix must go through `emit`/`materialize` rather than pushing an event directly.

Every OTHER `system` subtype â€” `init`, `task_started`, `task_updated`, `task_notification`, `background_tasks_changed`, and unknown subtypes â€” keeps its current Matriarch routing, asserted by a test that enumerates the subtypes present in `tests/fixtures/protocol/*.ndjson` and pins each one's destination. `task_started` in particular must NOT move: routing it to a Calf would force premature materialization.

A replay test over `01-parallel-dispatch.ndjson` asserts the 11 `task_progress` lines in the corpus land on the two Calves per their `tool_use_id`, that the two Calves' progress events do not cross, and that the Matriarch's event count drops by exactly the number of `task_progress` lines that resolved to a Calf.

Determinism and purity hold: replaying a fixture twice through freshly constructed routers with injected `newLaneId`/`now` yields byte-identical output, and `src/main/lane/` still imports neither `better-sqlite3`, `node:fs`, `electron`, nor the SDK. The existing `tests/router/purity.test.ts` and `determinism.test.ts` still pass unmodified.

`docs/known-issues/canusetool-attribution-race.md` exists and states, as a KNOWN LIMITATION and not as a fixed bug: that `canUseTool` is invoked out of band from stream ingestion; that both attribution indexes (`agentIds()` and `byToolUseId`) are populated only by ingesting `task_started` or the dispatch block; that a Calf's first tool prompt arriving before that ingestion falls back to the Matriarch and is indistinguishable from the correct no-id case; that the warning `PodManager.#attributePrompt` emits when a supplied id resolves to no lane is the ONLY observable signal; and that the two real fixes â€” awaiting ingestion of the owning dispatch, or parking the prompt until the lane materializes â€” are behavior changes deliberately out of scope for this session.

That document quotes the exact log text `#attributePrompt` emits and names the file and symbol, so a reader hitting the warning in a real log can find the code from the doc alone. If the fix in this task changes that log line, the doc quotes the new one.
The write-up is documentation only: no attribution behavior in `src/main/pod-manager/` is changed to work around the race, and no test is added that pretends to cover it.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both pass, including the full existing `tests/router/**` suite.

tasks.title: Renderer foundation: frozen contracts, design tokens, and the jsdom component-test harness
acceptance: The three frozen contract files are copied VERBATIM into `src/renderer/src/contracts/` and are the only definition of those types in the repo. They compile under `tsconfig.web.json` with `strict: true` and no `any` added to make them compile. They live under `src/renderer/`, not `src/shared/`, because `src/shared/**` is inside `tsconfig.node.json`'s include and these files import `react`.

`@testing-library/react` and `@testing-library/user-event` are added as devDependencies with pinned versions, alongside the already-installed `jsdom`. No RUNTIME dependency is added â€” `dependencies` stays exactly `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` and `better-sqlite3`. No styling library and no state-management library is added (resolved-unknowns U1, U4).
This task is the ONLY one that edits `package.json` or `package-lock.json`; every dependency the other renderer tasks need is declared here, so no later task touches either file.

`src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css` defines, on `:root`, every custom property named in `contracts/renderer-theme.ts`'s `TOKENS` â€” a test parses the CSS and asserts each token name appears exactly once as a definition, and that no token is defined that `TOKENS` does not name.

`src/renderer/src/styles/global.css` sets the app-level reset, the body background from `--oc-bg-app`, the UI font from `--oc-font-ui`, and a visible `:focus-visible` ring from `--oc-focus-ring`. It contains no component-specific selector: components style themselves through their own CSS Modules.

`src/renderer/src/test-utils/` exports a `renderWithWorkspace(ui, { api })` helper that mounts a component inside `WorkspaceProvider` with a supplied stub API, plus a `stubOrcastrateApi(overrides)` factory whose defaults resolve `{ ok: true }` envelopes for every invoke channel in `INVOKE_CHANNELS` and return working no-op `Unsubscribe` functions for every channel in `EVENT_CHANNELS`. A test enumerates both constant objects and asserts the stub covers every channel, so a stub cannot silently lag the frozen surface.

The stub factory exposes a way to DRIVE each push channel from a test (emit a `PodEventPush`, `LaneChangedPush`, `PermissionRequestedPush`, `PermissionResolvedPush`, `PodStatusPush`), and a way to make any invoke channel resolve `{ ok: false, error }` â€” the failure path is what the other tasks' acceptance criteria are written against.

At least one test file in this task carries the `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock and renders a React element successfully, proving the per-file jsdom opt-in `vitest.config.ts` already anticipates actually works. `vitest.config.ts` itself is NOT edited.
No file this task adds imports a `node:` builtin, `electron`, or `window.orcastrate` outside the stub's type position.
`npm install`, `npm test`, and `npm run typecheck` all pass on Windows from the state this task leaves behind.

tasks.title: App shell, Pod bar with drag-to-reorder, and the New Pod dialog
acceptance: `App.tsx` replaces the sub-session-1 placeholder entirely â€” no inline `style` object survives â€” and renders `WorkspaceLayout` with the Pod bar, and with the lane rail, transcript, split, and composer slots filled from the components T5, T6, and T7 provide. `main.tsx` mounts it inside `WorkspaceProvider` and imports `styles/global.css` exactly once.

`WorkspaceLayout` implements `WorkspaceLayoutProps` exactly: Pod bar across the top, lane rail on the left at `--oc-lane-rail-width`, transcript center, composer docked below (spec 5.1). When `split` is non-null the center region shows two side-by-side panes with `primary` on the left; when null it shows one.
The Pod bar renders one tab per `PodTabVm` in the array's order and does no sorting of its own. Each tab shows the user title and a status indicator colored from `statusToken(status)`.

Drag to reorder works and commits through `actions.reorderPods` with the FULL list in its new order; a test drags the third tab to first and asserts the single `reorderPods` call carries all ids in the new order. When the call fails, the bar reverts to the server order rather than keeping the dragged position.

A Pod with a pending permission request shows the `podTabPermissionBadge` element on its tab, and a test asserts the badge appears on a NON-ACTIVE Pod's tab â€” spec 5.4's entire point is that a backgrounded Pod waiting on the user is visible without switching to it.

A Pod created with `bypassPermissions` shows a persistent `podTabBypassBadge` whose accessible text is `BYPASS_PERMISSIONS_WARNING` verbatim â€” "This Pod will never ask you about anything." A test asserts that exact string. Generic danger wording fails this criterion: the SDK shadows `canUseTool` entirely in this mode, so such a Pod raises no permission cards at all, and a badge implying the user will still be asked about the dangerous things is false.

`+` opens the New Pod dialog, which collects title, working directory, permission mode, and optional env overrides. The directory is obtained ONLY via `actions.pickDirectory()` behind a Browse button and displayed read-only; a test asserts there is no editable input bound to `cwd` anywhere in the dialog, and that a cancelled pick (`{ path: null }`) leaves the dialog open with no error shown.

The dialog offers exactly the four modes in `PERMISSION_MODE_OPTIONS`, rendered from that array rather than a local literal list, each with its label and summary. Selecting `bypassPermissions` requires an explicit second confirmation before Create is enabled, and surfaces `BYPASS_PERMISSIONS_WARNING` in the `newPodBypassWarning` element.
Create is disabled until title is non-empty and `cwd` is set. On `{ ok: false }` from `createPod` the dialog stays open, shows `error.message` verbatim, and does not clear the user's input.
Every element listed under the Pod-bar and New-Pod entries of `TEST_IDS` carries that `data-testid`, suffixed per the contract, so T8's tests bind without having seen this markup.

No `window.orcastrate` call, no `node:` import, and no hardcoded color, font, or spacing literal appears in this task's files â€” every visual value is `var(--oc-â€¦)` from `TOKENS`. Styling is CSS Modules co-located in this task's own directories.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

tasks.title: Workspace state layer: the only caller of window.orcastrate, implementing the renderer-state contract
acceptance: `src/renderer/src/state/` implements `WorkspaceProvider`, `useWorkspace`, `usePods`, `usePodSession`, `useLaneRail`, `useTranscript`, `useComposer`, `usePermissionCards`, `useWorkspaceActions`, and `steerPrefill` from `contracts/renderer-state.ts` exactly â€” every member present with the contract's signature, none added, none removed.
This is the ONLY directory in `src/renderer/` that references `window.orcastrate`; a test greps the renderer tree and fails if any other file does.

No action ever rejects or throws. A test forces EVERY invoke channel to resolve `{ ok: false }` in turn and asserts the corresponding action resolves `{ ok: false, error }` with the same `IpcError` object passed through unmodified. A second test makes a channel's promise reject outright and asserts the action still resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `INTERNAL`, because a preload bug must not become an unhandled rejection.

Locally detected precondition failures never reach IPC and surface as `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: sending empty or whitespace-only composer text, and denying a permission with an empty or whitespace-only reason. Both are asserted to have made zero IPC calls.

The provider subscribes to all five `EVENT_CHANNELS` exactly once on mount and calls every returned `Unsubscribe` on unmount â€” asserted by mounting, unmounting, and checking each unsubscribe ran exactly once, then emitting a push and asserting no state update follows.

Transcript merge is correct and is the criterion this task lives or dies on: `TranscriptView.events` is strictly ascending by `seq`, has no duplicate `seq`, and is append-stable. A test interleaves a live `PodEventPush` carrying seq 40-45 with a backfill page that later returns seq 1-100 and asserts the result contains each seq exactly once, in order, with nothing dropped.

Backfill pages forward via `events.read` using `afterSeq` and stops on `hasMore === false` rather than on a short page; concurrent `loadMoreEvents` calls coalesce into one in-flight request. `pageSize` above 5000 is not treated as an error â€” main clamps it â€” and the resulting shorter page does not end paging.

`LaneChangedPush` replaces the lane list wholesale, as the snapshot the frozen contract says it is: a push omitting a previously-known lane removes that lane's row. The rail order guarantee holds â€” Matriarch at index 0 always, Calves by `startedAt` then `id`, and a lane that changes only status does not move.

A permission card is removed when, and only when, a `permissionResolved` push arrives for its `requestId` â€” including outcome `'aborted'`, which clears the card silently with no error state. A test asserts the card is NOT removed optimistically on click, that a failed `respond` leaves it visible with `error` set and `submitting` false, and that a `permissionResolved` for an unknown `requestId` is a no-op.

Selection and pin invariants hold: `pinnedLaneId !== selectedLaneId` at all times; pinning the selected lane is a no-op; selecting the pinned lane swaps the panes instead of closing the split; at most one lane is pinned. Asserted by a test that exercises each transition.

`steerPrefill` returns null for a lane with no `agentId`, and otherwise a string beginning with `STEER_PREFILL_PREFIX` and naming the agent id â€” asserted verbatim. `steerFromLane` writes it into the Pod composer and sends nothing; a test asserts zero `pods.send` calls result.

`routingMode` is read once from `app.routingMode()` and exposed unchanged; the state layer contains no branch that assumes `'lanes'`. Unread counts behave as specified: zero for the active Pod and for the selected lane at all times.
No `node:` import, no filesystem path composed or parsed â€” `cwd` is passed through as an opaque string and only ever originates from `pickDirectory`.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

tasks.title: Lane rail, streaming transcript, inline dispatch card, and the pinned split pane
acceptance: The lane rail implements `LaneRailProps` and renders a LIST, not a second tab row (spec 5.1): Matriarch pinned at the top, Calves beneath, each row showing agent type, description, status, elapsed time, and an unread indicator. A test asserts the Matriarch is the first row even when the supplied array is shuffled by the caller.

Elapsed time comes from `LaneRowVm.elapsedMs` and is formatted for display only â€” no row runs its own timer or reads the clock, so a finished lane's row stops re-rendering. A test renders a `done` lane with fake timers, advances them, and asserts no re-render.
Pin and unpin are wired to `onPin`/`onUnpin`, and `Steer` is offered only on rows whose lane has an `agentId`; a test asserts the `laneRowSteer` control is absent for a lane with `agentId: null`.

The transcript implements `TranscriptPaneProps` and renders the selected lane's events in `seq` order, one element per event carrying `testId(TEST_IDS.transcriptEvent, seq)`. Each `EventType` in the frozen union has a rendering â€” including `malformed`, which renders the raw line visibly rather than being skipped (spec 8), and `error`, which shows the exit code when present.

New events appended by a live push land at the bottom without re-mounting existing event elements, and the pane auto-scrolls only when the user is already at the bottom â€” a test asserts a scrolled-up reader is not yanked down by an incoming event.
The backfill affordance calls `onLoadMore` and is hidden when `hasMore` is false; it is never shown as an error when a page returns fewer rows than requested.

The inline dispatch card renders at the position in the Matriarch transcript where the dispatch fired (spec 5.2), showing "dispatched N agents" with one row per opened lane carrying that lane's status, and clicking a row calls `onJumpToLane` with that lane's id. A test asserts the count text for a three-agent dispatch.

The card is detected by `payload.dispatchedLaneId !== undefined`, NOT by the tool name. A test feeds a `tool_use` event whose `name` is `'Agent'` and another whose `name` is `'Task'` and asserts both render a card â€” the dispatch tool is `Agent` on CLI 2.1.235 and `Task` on older ones, and a name check written against either alone silently renders zero cards.

In `routingMode: 'inline'` the card still renders with its count and no per-agent rows rather than disappearing, and the rail does not present lane selection as if it filtered the transcript. A test drives both routing modes through the same component and asserts neither branch is hardcoded.

The pinned split pane renders a second `TranscriptPane` with `isSplit: true`, without its own composer â€” there is one composer per Pod, not per pane (spec 5.2). A test asserts the split pane contains no `composerInput`.

`permissionSlot` is rendered inside the transcript's scroll container, at the end of the lane's event stream, and this task renders nothing about its contents â€” a test passes a sentinel node and asserts it appears inside the pane rather than in a portal or overlay.
Every element named in the lane-rail, transcript, and dispatch-card entries of `TEST_IDS` carries that `data-testid`.
No `window.orcastrate` call, no `node:` import, no hardcoded color, font, or spacing literal; CSS Modules only, tokens only.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

tasks.title: Pod composer with Esc-to-interrupt, and the inline permission cards
acceptance: The composer implements `ComposerProps` and is bound to the POD, not the lane (spec 5.2): a test selects a different lane and asserts the composer's text is unchanged and that it is still enabled while a read-only Calf lane is selected. There is exactly one composer per Pod.

Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Send is disabled while `state.sending` is true and while `state.disabled` is true; when disabled, the composer shows text derived from `disabledReason` rather than silently swallowing input. A test asserts a click while sending produces no second `onSend`.
`Esc` with the composer focused calls `onInterrupt` and does NOT clear the draft â€” a test types text, presses Esc, and asserts the text survives and `onInterrupt` fired exactly once (spec 5.4).
The composer renders `state.error.message` verbatim when a send failed, and the message clears on the next edit.

Prefilled Steer text arrives through `ComposerState.text` like any other value â€” this task neither formats the prefill string nor calls `steerPrefill`; a test asserts a prefilled composer renders the string it was handed and focuses the input.

Permission cards implement `PermissionCardListProps` and render INLINE, in document flow, in the lane that asked. A test asserts the card is not a modal: no element rendered by this task has `position: fixed`, an overlay backdrop, or a `role="dialog"` that traps focus, and content behind it stays reachable.

Each card shows the tool name and the request input, and offers exactly three actions: Allow, Allow always, and Deny with reason. Allow and Allow always call `onRespond` with the decision and no reason.

Deny is DISABLED until the reason field holds non-whitespace text, so the user cannot click into an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` round trip. A test asserts the disabled state with an empty reason, with a whitespace-only reason, and that `onRespond` carries the trimmed reason once enabled.
All three buttons are disabled while `card.submitting` is true, so a double-click cannot send two decisions for one `requestId` â€” asserted by a test that clicks twice and counts one `onRespond`.

A card with `error` set stays on screen showing `error.message` with its buttons re-enabled â€” it does not disappear, because the request is genuinely still unanswered. A card is never removed by this component; removal is the state layer's, driven by `permissionResolved`. A test asserts clicking Allow does not remove the card from the DOM by itself.
Cards render oldest first and are keyed by `requestId`, so a card resolving out of order does not remount its siblings.
Every element named in the composer and permission entries of `TEST_IDS` carries that `data-testid`.
No `window.orcastrate` call, no `node:` import, no hardcoded color, font, or spacing literal; CSS Modules only, tokens only.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

tasks.title: Renderer integration test suite over the assembled workspace
acceptance: Every test file lives under `src/renderer/src/__tests__/` and carries a `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock. Nothing is added under `tests/`, because `tests/**` is inside `tsconfig.node.json`'s include and a `.tsx` renderer test there fails the node typecheck.

The suite mounts the FULL app â€” `main.tsx`'s tree, not individual components â€” against `stubOrcastrateApi`, and drives it entirely through `TEST_IDS` and user-visible text. No test reaches into a component's internal state or imports a non-exported symbol.

End-to-end path, asserted as one test: stub `pods.list` with two Pods, click the second tab, drive a `LaneChangedPush` with a Matriarch and two Calves, drive a `PodEventPush`, and assert the rail lists three rows in the guaranteed order and the transcript shows the pushed events in `seq` order.

Permission path, asserted end to end: drive a `PermissionRequestedPush` for a CALF lane, assert the card renders inside that Calf's transcript and NOT in the Matriarch's; assert the asking Pod's tab shows the permission badge while a DIFFERENT Pod is active; click Deny with an empty reason and assert nothing was sent; type a reason, deny, and assert one `permissions.respond` call with the trimmed reason; then drive `permissionResolved` and assert the card and the tab badge both clear.
Aborted path: drive a `PermissionRequestedPush`, then a `permissionResolved` with outcome `'aborted'` without any user action, and assert the card disappears with no error text anywhere on screen.

Failure path: make every invoke channel resolve `{ ok: false }` in turn and assert the app renders the error message and stays interactive â€” no blank window, no unhandled rejection. A test installs a `window.onunhandledrejection` spy for the whole suite and fails if it ever fires.

Wording assertions the product depends on, asserted verbatim rather than by substring: `BYPASS_PERMISSIONS_WARNING` appears in both the New Pod dialog's bypass option and the created Pod's tab badge; the Steer prefill string produced for a Calf with an `agentId` matches `steerPrefill`'s output exactly and no `pods.send` results from clicking Steer.

`PERMISSION_MODE_OPTIONS` is asserted exhaustive over the widened `PermissionMode` union by a type-level check plus a runtime assertion that the dialog renders one option per union member â€” not by asserting the literal number four.

Security hygiene, as executable assertions over the source tree: no file under `src/renderer/**` imports a `node:` builtin, `electron`, or `better-sqlite3`; no file outside `src/renderer/src/state/**` references `window.orcastrate`; no file under `src/renderer/**` outside `styles/` contains a hex color, an `rgb(`/`hsl(` literal, a `px` font-size, or a hardcoded font stack. Modelled on the existing `tests/router/hygiene.test.ts`.
Unmount cleanliness: mounting and unmounting the app calls every `Unsubscribe` the stub handed out exactly once, and a push delivered after unmount updates nothing and throws nothing.
No test spawns a process, opens a network connection, touches SQLite, requires an API key, or reads a real filesystem path.
The suite is part of the default `npm test` run, not behind an opt-in flag, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

tasks.title: Open and reconnect an existing Pod from the UI
acceptance: A Pod that is listed but not opened offers a visible, keyboard-operable control that calls actions.openPod(podId). A test asserts exactly one openPod call carrying that Pod's id.
A Pod whose status is 'beached' offers a control that calls actions.reconnectPod(podId) instead. A test asserts reconnectPod, not openPod, is the call for that status.
The control is absent, or unambiguously inert, for a Pod that is already open - a test asserts no openPod call is reachable for an opened Pod.
On a failed open the Pod stays listed and the error message renders verbatim; the app stays interactive and no unhandled rejection occurs. Asserted by forcing podOpen to resolve not-ok.
After a successful open the composer for that Pod becomes enabled - the disabledReason 'not-opened' no longer renders. Asserted end to end through the assembled app.

The integration suite gains a restart-shaped test: pods.list returns Pods with opened false, and the suite drives the new control to reach a sendable composer. This is the scenario the session's definition of done omitted.
No window.orcastrate call outside state/, no node: import, no hardcoded color, font, or spacing literal; CSS Modules and TOKENS only.
npm test and npm run typecheck both pass.
